name: secrets
description: Credentials and keys committed to the source: private keys, cloud and chat tokens, literal passwords.

rules.title: A private key is in the source
rules.why: A private key in a repository is readable by everyone who can read the repository, and stays in its history.
rules.fix: Remove it, rotate the key, and load keys from a secret store or the environment.

rules.title: An AWS access key id
rules.why: An access key id in the source identifies a credential, and is usually next to its secret.
rules.fix: Revoke the key, and use an instance role or the environment.

rules.title: A GitHub token
rules.why: A personal, OAuth or app token grants whatever its owner could do on GitHub.
rules.fix: Revoke it on GitHub and read tokens from the environment or a secret store.

rules.title: A Slack token
rules.why: A Slack token lets whoever holds it act as the bot or user it was issued to.
rules.fix: Revoke it in Slack and load it from the environment.

rules.title: A key or secret assigned a literal
rules.why: A literal key in the source is shared with everyone who can read it and cannot be rotated without a change.
rules.fix: Read it from the environment or a secret store.

rules.title: A password assigned a literal
rules.why: A literal password in the source is a credential everyone with the code has.
rules.fix: Read it from the environment or a secret store; never commit a real one, even for a test database.

rules.title: A user name and password inside a URL
rules.why: Credentials in a URL end up in logs, process listings, error messages and shell history.
rules.fix: Pass credentials separately (a header, a client option, the environment).
